html:
Ecotourism is travel to see nature, and Costa Rica became its best-known example from the 1970s. Its national parks and reserves now cover about a quarter of the country.

In the 1960s and 1970s cattle ranching and banana farming were clearing Costa Rica's forests fast. A national park service was set up around 1970, and reserves such as Monteverde in the cloud forest drew scientists and then tourists. From 1996 the state paid landowners to keep forest standing, and forest cover recovered from its low point in the 1980s to over half the country.

Tourism became a leading source of foreign money, much of it from people who come to see sloths, quetzals, volcanoes and turtle beaches. The country is often cited as a case where protecting nature paid, unlike the cleared land of the banana coasts or the Amazon frontier.
sum: Ecotourism is travel to see nature, and Costa Rica became its best-known example from the 1970s. Its national parks and reserves now cover about a quarter of the country.
